utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (In French) Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't seem to be getting any English translation, but, Mr. Nice, if you would like to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I expect it will come.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlotrg, just a few outstanding matters for one other occasion you can tell us about at some stage, and you may have to help us with the date, involving a cafe and some HVO soldiers, when you were at the cafe in the course of work?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I think this was on the 18th of May, 1992. As I was going back from work, I noticed some members of the reserve police force in front of a cafe that was owned by Gojko Cickovic. I walked up to my colleague and asked him whether he needed any help, and I wanted to ask him what it was all about. He said that no help was needed and that I should leave. From there, I went to my brother's, that is to say, my brother who was killed on the 16th of April, I went to his apartment. After some time, members of the HVO rang the doorbell at my brother's apartment. My brother and I went out, and we saw Mr. Mario Cerkez there accompanied by three soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council. They were armed with automatic rifles. One of them had a machine gun, and he pointed it at my stomach. I moved the barrel away and I asked Mario what all of this was supposed to mean. "I'm a member of the police force, and it is I and my colleagues who can come to somebody's door, not members of the Croatian Defence Council." I also draw his attention to the fact that he shouldn't do that any more. He said, approximately, that he would come to the door whenever he wanted to and, if necessary, he would bring a company of members of the Croatian Defence Council and that nobody could prevent him from doing so. He just told me not to talk to members of the Croatian Defence Council any more, and I told him that this was a policeman who should not be under his command. However -- well, this is the way I understood him, that I had nothing to talk to Croats about. Later on I found out that a group from the reserve police force from the reserve police station that was in Bila and which was commanded by Ivan Budimir and their zone of responsibility was supposed -- or, rather, they were supposed to protect law and order in the villages around Stara Bila in keeping with the set-up of the Vitez police station, that is to say, Mosunj, Veliki Mosunj, Sadovace, Grbavica and that part; they had nothing to do in town. However, Ivan Budimir gave these people as assistants to Mario Cerkez. On that occasion, they expelled Dragan Cickovic who was running that cafe, and they simply took the cafe for the needs of the Croatian Defence Council. Dragan later told me that Mario had told him that the cafe was being taken away for the needs of the Croatian Defence Council, that is to say, for the families of the members from Mosunj who were killed. They did not make an inventory of all the goods that were in the cafe on that occasion nor did they issue any kind of certificate. They simply ordered Dragan to leave the premises, and they handed this establishment to Tomic Zoka, I think his name was, and he was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did that cafe then remain in the possession of a particular group or party thereafter?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: After that, in the cafe, members of the Croatian Defence Council in uniform would meet at the cafe, and as far as I know, until the conflict broke out, it was owned by the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Was that the only example of Croat properties being -- I beg your pardon -- Muslim properties being occupied by Croats, or were there others?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not the only example.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What sort of number of others were there, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that when I was presenting this general overview and when I mentioned that they were taking our vehicles away, they mostly blew up cafes rather than taking them away, and after all, this cafe that they took was not owned by a Muslim but it was owned by a Serb. I talked about it just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the end of the time, in 1993, how many Muslims remained in Vitez then, if you can express it in any terms or in percentage terms?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I fled from Vitez on the 16th of May, I think that 50 or 60 per cent remained in Vitez; however, by the end of 1993, I believe that there weren't even 10 per cent in Vitez. All the rest were expelled or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were still there --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: ... killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were still there, was there aid, food aid in particular, coming through or to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: While I was in custody, my wife said that on several occasions they brought food in front of the entrance and they only distributed food to Croats and Serbs. At that time, the three children of my brother who was killed together with his wife, they came over to stay with me at my apartment together with their grandmother, so there was five of them, and then these neighbours asked to have some food given to the children because there were so many children there. However, the Croat who was doing this said that there was nothing for the balijas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You told us one or two incidents of what happened to you when you were doing your work as a police officer. Just in a sentence, when you were doing your work as a police officer, how were you treated generally when you went to the scenes of crimes and so on?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: If an offence was committed on territory that went beyond Stari Vitez and if we had to go through territory that was under HVO control, until I would reach the scene, I would -- or not only myself but the entire investigating team would be taken out of our vehicles, we would be searched, we would have to put our hands up, and then they would search the vehicle too and then they would let us go. At one point in time, or, actually, when we were involved in one particular investigation, when one of our men stepped on a mine between Tolovici and, I think, Krcevine or Preocica, we agreed with our colleagues from the police station that we could pass. We passed one checkpoint because we persuaded them to let us go. The other checkpoint, which was 100 metres away from the first one and you can see it, the guards from the other checkpoint saw us pass the first checkpoint; however, the guard again made us leave the vehicle, went to headquarters to see whether we could pass, and he returned later and he said that we should go back, that he cannot let us go to the scene to investigate. And that's the way it was every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. I should have asked you this earlier: Were you yourself active in politics at all, active in the SDA or in any other way?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I should also have asked you to deal with telephones. You told us somebody came and took your telephone before the time when you were finally arrested. Was that seizing of telephones unique to you, or did it happen to others, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they took the telephones of all Muslims, and then when they would leave the building, they would throw the telephones on the concrete and break them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So although telephones were taken, were you still able to watch the television?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The man, Anto Valenta, you made reference to him yesterday and to his book. Did you know him at all?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What were his expressed views on things?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you can see that from the book too. He changed the boundaries of municipalities on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He proposed humane resettlements. He simply annexed to one municipality villages with a Croat population so that he would create or, rather, not create but he actually wanted to have an imbalance between the Croats and the Muslims, one that would be in favour of the Croats. At press conferences that were held in Busovaca, he said that in public on several occasions, and he showed us maps of Travnik and explained them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was his position in the HDZ at the time; do you know?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was a high political official. I don't know exactly what he was, but I know that he was in the top echelons in the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You have told us about Stari Vitez itself and you have also used the word "Mahala." "Mahala" I think turns up in relation to a number of towns or villages. Can you just explain the position and, in particular, the ethnic composition of Stari Vitez and whether the name "Mahala" has any general significance for the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: "Mahala" is a Turkish word that relates to a particular section of town, and in Stari Vitez, the majority population was Muslim. However, I should also like to add that our Croat neighbours who did not want to be exchanged spent the entire war in Stari Vitez. They were treated like everyone else. That was the Pavlovic family, then the Mioc family and, I don't know, some other families too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. The mosque in Stari Vitez, what happened to that and when? You have touched on this already.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: In '92, at a joint meeting, rather, on a mission where Pero Skopljak was and a priest, I don't know his name, on one side, and on the other side was Mr. Munib Kajmovic and Omer Mestrovac, the hodza of Vitez. Then Pero Skopljak said publicly that he had ordered the shelling of the minaret of the Vitez mosque because, allegedly, that is what he said, there was a sniper that was operating from up there, and then, on several occasions, the hodza of Vitez swore that there were no snipers on top of the minaret and then Pero Skopljak told him that he was lying, something to that effect, and I know that Jurcevic, called Butur, was shooting from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was it possible thereafter to pray publicly for Muslims or not; what was the position?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The mosque was in Stari Vitez, that is to say, that it was possible, but then how risky this was, that's another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The man, Bralo, of whom you spoke yesterday, did he make some particular boast of what he had done on one occasion?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. When we were digging trenches, when they brought us to dig trenches, he said that he was involved in a competition in killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he give one detail of a particular killing he had engaged in, he had done?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He said that the hajji who had built the mosque in the lower part of Ahmici, that he had crucified him like Jesus, and that when he crucified him, he put nails into his hands and his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he say where he had done that?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember, but it was on the door of some place. I don't know whether it was on the door of the mosque or the door of a house. I really can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you aware of any particular paramilitary groups in or around Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not aware of paramilitary groups because all units were under the control, the Jokers and everybody were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Under the control of whom?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's all I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Who is to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: We would like to start over here with co-counsel first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I trust that means you are applying to do that because you are changing the usual order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Exactly, sir, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I take it that the burden of cross-examination will be on Mr. Kovacic because this involves Vitez; is that right? So you will be much shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: In all ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zlotrg. I am the defence counsel for Mario Cerkez, and I have a few questions to put to you. In view of the breadth of your testimony, there's going to be quite a bit of it, so I ask you to be patient. Yesterday, you said that you started to work in the Ministry of the Interior in the early '80s, and then you said that it was actually in 1986; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think it was in 1986. After all, this can be found in the archives of the Ministry of the Interior. You can check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Then we agree that you started working there in the mid '80s; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What schools did you complete or, rather, when you started working in the police force, what schools had you finished?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I worked as a car mechanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In order to work as a car mechanic, what did you complete?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I completed a secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So that was a secondary school?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It was a vocational school?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In your day, it lasted three years?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is to say, you went to an eight-year elementary school, a three-year vocational school, and then you started working in the police force; right? And in 1986, you got a job at the Ministry of the Interior for the first time?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, it's hard to define this, but can I say that you were actually in charge of stocks and other equipment that the Ministry of the Interior had?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Including weapons, ammunition, equipment for the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The active force too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I see. For the active and reserve police force. Thank you. At the point in time when you started working at the MUP in Vitez, who was the head of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Hazim Viteskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Hazim Viteskic, he was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At that time, for example, the first year, two or three that you spent working there, do you remember what the ethnic composition was in the MUP, that is to say, the ethnic composition of employees?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I could not tell you for sure but it was quite balanced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did this composition reflect the ethnic composition or structure of the population of the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think so but I'm not a politician. Before the conflict, I didn't know what these percentages were, how many Muslims or how many Croats or how many Serbs lived in Vitez, so I can't really tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me rephrase the question. May I conclude that you did not feel that things were different in the police station than they were in regular life in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were there any serious deviations from that, you probably would have felt it; right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that certain changes took place in the MUP, that Mr. Pero Skopljak became head of the MUP, that the commander was changed too, and now who became the commander?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Saban Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: He was not commander until before the elections?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, Skopljak wasn't head of police either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please, just give me "Yes" or "No" answers. I'm going to ask you about that further on.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: After the elections, you got two new bosses, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your top boss was the head of the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The lower boss, so to speak, "a bit lower," but we just need to understand each other, was Mahmutovic; right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mahmutovic commanded the uniformed part, that is to say, the authorised officials, and the head of MUP had authorised and unauthorised officials under him, that is to say, that the police is a semi-military organisation which does have a system of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. So from the point of view of hierarchy, is it correct, what I said?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So Pero Skopljak was top man and --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Below him was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. This set-up of the leading positions, was it rather a result of the key positions in the municipality after the coalition and the HDZ had won the elections?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think so, but I was not a member of any political party, so I can't give you any answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You don't have any firsthand knowledge about this?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that's the way I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Who did you replace as logistics officer?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I said, in 1986, it was Edin Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. You told us then that you were transferred, or you, rather, used the word "replaced," as logistics officer and that you were reassigned to the post of criminology technician?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the organisation of work at the police station, in the sense of pay, salary, job descriptions at the police station, who is better paid?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that criminology technicians are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So a criminology technician is a person who has a better position than a logistics officer; right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but it requires a lot more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Does it also require more expertise and more knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, definitely, because this is a very specialised job, and you have to focus on certain activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me summarise this. It is a more complex job in terms of job description and has a higher salary, it requires better qualifications, and you're saying, nevertheless, that you were replaced from the position of logistics officer?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Wasn't it perhaps some kind of a promotion or perhaps a reassignment?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it would have been for you, but I was on the losing end because I could earn far more by doing second jobs moonlighting than through this salary, because I was on duty around the clock, seven days a week, and then I would rest for seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand this, as technician or what?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, as technician, I was on duty for seven days, round the clock, when it was my turn to be on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And as logistics officer?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I would work my eight-hour working day and then would be free.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But if I understood you correctly, then you would make more money during your free time?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I worked as a car mechanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I've been warned, and I'm asking you to do the same thing. We shouldn't overlap one another. Let's wait for the interpreters to interpret what we've said, and then let's finish. So that was why you were appointed to the job of a criminology technician as a replacement, it was something that was better for you?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Otherwise, one could say it was a promotion, by all other standards?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't ask for it. It was Mr. Skopljak who insisted on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you were assigned to do the job of technician, did you have the training necessary for this?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I immediately proceeded to Sarajevo to a course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: How long were you at that course?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, two months, two and a half months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was it a serious course where you worked a lot?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was also a crash course because of the situation, so that we really worked practically the whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the Ministry of the Interior School at Vraca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. There, did you acquire at least some basic knowledge about how one calculates the angle of the bouncing bullet or what?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. That was a matter for experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And criminology technicians, they don't go through that kind of training?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Ours was only to find traces to take -- to put on record all the marks or whatever and file them and, of course, measure some parameters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you do know which are relevant marks and things like that, otherwise you should know how to calculate an angle?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we never calculated the angle. We never learned that, but we did learn the bullet trajectories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You learned the trajectories?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you learn anything about how to differentiate between projectiles fired from semi-automatics and automatic weapons, on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we did not learn anything about that difference, and I don't think there was any need to. As for calibres of weapons, weapon calibres, we were not the ones who ascertained that on a victim. Others do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the bullet casings found there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, when you find them, you send them to an expert for the expert analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you well, that your training came down to the framework needed for a technician to secure marks and evidence?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you all that we were taught there if you were interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No. It will be easier this way.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, we could establish -- of course, find traces of gunpowder on clothes and all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No. Just let it be. Let me just try to finish with this part.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is what I'm telling you. We can establish the relevant distance, whether it was at close range or not, judging by the gunpowder marks on the body and so on and so forth, but I simply do not think that this is -- I'm really not passing a test for a criminology technician right now, am I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a specific question. Yesterday, you told us about the on-site investigation when Samir Trako was killed, and you mentioned a detail. You said that there was an entry and an exit hole on the glass or you said two or three holes had been made in the glass pane and that you were worried or, rather, that you were puzzled. How could it be that on the other glass pane, which was on the other side, there were no holes or any other mark?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Tell us, how could you conclude since you didn't know where the shot had been fired from?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course we knew where the fire had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: How did you?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the basis of what we were shown by the commander of the military police. The shot came from a distance of some five or six metres away from Trako.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And that was roughly where?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The desk or the table at which members of the Croatian Defence were sitting and Perica Vukadinovic was sitting there at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And that was supposed to be a reception desk or something?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not the reception desk because that was in the hall, and that was over here in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It served as an office or what?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, please, Mr. Zlotrg, in the former Yugoslavia or in Bosnia, did you ever act as an expert witness in court, as a criminology expert?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've already told you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No. Tell me "Yes" or "No" before the Court.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I became a criminology technician much later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you never testified as an expert witness?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the former Yugoslavia, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Since we are addressing this issue, that is, the investigation of the killing of the late Samir Trako, I should like to clarify certain matters so I do have a few questions in this regard. You go into the hotel. As far as I remember, there is a glass door, two openings, and then behind it is another glass door; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: And between them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And between them is a passage. Then beyond that second glass door is a corridor where there is a cloakroom?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And from that corridor, stairs lead downstairs --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- to the bowling hall. And there was a bar in the bowling hall?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but it wasn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It was a public place?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Any visitor could go there, those who did. But it is true that the late Samir Trako and his two colleagues, Petar and another Trako --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I didn't hear his name.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- were also there that night. That is what we know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you learn during the investigation that the three of them were in that bar?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you learn that some other people, including Muslims, were in that bar?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: To my knowledge, there were members of the Croatian Defence Council, and I'm not aware of anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But just now, you told us that there were HVO members, and a while ago, you also said there were some other people. Now we've got -- well, in addition to the three of them --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: In addition to the three of them, that's what I said. I told you -- I confirmed that the three of them were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So we agree that that particular bar was open to all?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I know that I did not go there because nobody invited me there. But, yes, I agree --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But most of the Muslims were not desirable there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But was it open to all?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I guess so. I did not go there, so I really can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One moment. A pause between question and answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Sir, that evening, from what you are saying, at least those three, that is, two Trakos and Petak, were there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And they were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are Muslims. It's not that they were, they are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I said "were" because one of them was killed. You also confirmed that there were some other individuals there about whom you learned later.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You told us that in the hotel building or, rather, in that office, there was, you told us, the HVO command and you said also Cerkez's post, that he worked there, allegedly, and you also added that you didn't know in what capacity Cerkez was in that institution.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said -- I said that it was a commander, but I do not know whether it would be a gauge of the staff or what because I do not know how the HVO was organised at the time, but I do know that a couple of months later, we saw the Vitez Brigade and that Mr. Cerkez took over the duty of the commander. That is what I know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I do not think we should now go back to the transcript to see what you said or did not say. I do not think that you said a commander, I think you said "I don't know in what capacity." But we do have a transcript so it doesn't really matter. Since you mentioned the alignment of the brigade, do you remember when that happened?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know it was a warm day. I subsequently later [as interpreted] that a couple of combatants dropped down and Dr. Mujezinovic with his team had to extend for a stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it was summer '92. And you said that Mario Cerkez then became the commander of what?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of the Vitez Brigade, from what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of the Vitez Brigade or the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that the Vitez Brigade existed at that time?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I cannot talk about the organisation of the army of the Croatian Defence Council because I had no access to that, but on the basis of all the other developments, that was my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And that alignment, was it secret, public?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were the police members there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Live Note is finding the speed very difficult or impossible to keep up with.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I add a detail that the Live Note transcribers asked me to mention? The particular problem this morning includes, or problems this morning include, that the interpreters aren't identifying the end of question and answer by use of the word "Question," "Answer"; and therefore, it is very difficult for her to distinguish, in typing the text, so on, which is the question from which is the answer. I only make these points on her behalf because I am sitting next to her and we discovered that she was in difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, let me explain what I think the problem is. Because you speak the same language as the witness, you tend to have a kind of conversation, and so the questions and the answers are intermingled, and so quite often we see here, "Can't distinguish between questions and answer." And that doesn't help us. So I think you will have to make a very determined effort to slow down and to ensure that the witness answers you before you move on to the next question and I think the witness also has to be aware of the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will do my best. As you said rightly, my problem is that we are speaking the same language and then I reflectly (sic) and the witness is also doing so, then we both probably should try. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Zlotrg, you heard it just as well as I did. With regard to this investigation, you mentioned Mr. Efraim Pinjo.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He was assistant commander of the Territorial Defence for security matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you. Could you please now see a video recording, with the Court's permission? Your Honours, I should merely like to ask the witness to identify the gentleman that we just referred to. It's about five seconds or ten seconds of video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at it and then tell us whether this is Efraim Pinjo?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: THE INTERPRETER (Voiceover): "INTERVIEWER: Here in Travnik we found Mr. Efraim Pinjo. Once upon a time, he worked for the TO in Vitez. We shall ask him to tell us under what conditions did he move to Travnik, why did he leave Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MR. PINJO
utterances.text: I moved to Travnik because I was driven away. People were also sent away. The former colleague, Hakija Cengic and others and those who drove a [indiscernible] also my fellow policemen, Croats, they know very well who we are and those who were driven away were sent to Zenica. INTERVIEWER: And what are you doing here? Here you are with the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PINJO
utterances.text: Yes, I am here with the joint command. This is what I also wanted to do. INTERVIEWER: That command has [indiscernible] of May. How has it been working?

utterances.speaker: MR. PINJO
utterances.text: Well, so far it's been all right, and this joint command will defend my city and their city too. INTERVIEWER: Thank you. Thank you."

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is Efraim Pinjo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Excuse me. Could we please have this admitted as an exhibit for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you have a date for it, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) No, unfortunately, we do not, but I think the witness might tell us. I will ask him when did Efraim Pinjo leave Vitez and go to Travnik. We heard him say that he did so. This is material from different places and, unfortunately, there is simply odds and ends, and most of them do not have that particular marking on the tape, although I think he does mention May, early May, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Interpretation) This will be number D3/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) May I go on, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zlotrg, this is Efraim Pinjo who you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So he was a security officer with the Territorial Defence headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Assistant commander?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when he left Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know when he left because I was not in the army then, but this recording must have been made while we were still on very friendly relations with the Croatian Defence Council in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could it be early May '92?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. You'd have to ask him. I suppose he knows when he made the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you exclude the possibility it was May 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: It could have been any time before the conflict in Travnik between the HVO and the Armija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What was the connection between the reserve police force with the Territorial Defence, subsequently the army of the B and H?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The reserve police force was subordinated to the commander and through the commander to the chief, and if the commanders agreed a coordinated action with the Armija, then they did it. If not, then each one would do his job. I mean, the reserve police, of course, was responsible for public order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that the officer on duty at the station, after you received information about the murder in the hotel, did not call you to take part in the investigation, he called up the chief?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And then another team went?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the one that was appointed by the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see, the one who was appointed by the chief. Tell me, this murder, at that time, was that a delicate matter for the police in view of the tensions, inter-ethnic tensions, in the community?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: In May? Well, it shouldn't have been. If I could go to Kruscica later and if I could receive information about the murder after one hour only, I don't see why it couldn't have gone a few months before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, so in May 1992, there were no inter-ethnic tensions?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were tensions, but they did not reach that point where an investigation could not be carried out. Perhaps it was a different backdrop against --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, so you think that the duty officer at the police station, this chief, could have resolved that matter routinely?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The duty officer was not supposed to inform the chief at all. He did not have to. First he was supposed to inform the investigating team and then to take this telegram to the chief for his signature and then to inform him about the event. Why did he not inform the commander of the station, who was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. At any rate, you performed the investigation the next morning; right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read some names to you, so could you please confirm whether these people were there? On the next morning, was investigating judge of the basic court in Travnik, Mr. Zeljko Percinlic, was he there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So he was. What about the operations workers of the Public Security Station of Vitez, Salem Topcic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What are these men, ethnically speaking?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Vlado is a Croat, and he was there the night before that, and Salem, who came only on that morning, he was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So from the Public Security Station of Vitez, one Muslim and one Croat?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: As a criminology technician from the same station, you were present and Frano Sucic was present?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but Frano was there that night too and I was not. I only came on the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. But that morning, you were there and Frano was there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You told us that you were a Muslim or a Bosniak, ethnically, you.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And Frano?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Frano is a Croat. I imagine that he says he's a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I know it sounds a bit strange. The two of us know but others don't. That's why I had to ask this question so that it would be in the transcript. Then Vlado Miskovic was present, the public prosecutor from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, so he was there. A few minutes ago, a person who was mentioned who we saw on the video clip too, Pinjo Efraim; was he there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is to say that there was a total of seven persons there in this official capacity?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. But the crime scene was not secured properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Please, we'll take things one at a time and we'll reach that. At this point I would like to ask the Court the following: I have this document. I have the record of this investigation, but I owe you an explanation. Witness Zlotrg was supposed to testify only after the next witnesses who are supposed to come in. I'm not going to mention their names because I don't know what their status will be and how they will testify. So that is to say, the three witnesses were skipped. Immediately on the 26th, when our colleague from the Prosecution told us that this witness will be brought in instead of the planned witnesses, we asked the registry for a translation of this document. Of course, I have a copy here of the request. We asked that this be done as soon as possible; however, unfortunately, this has not been done by this morning, but I would like to ask you nevertheless that we use this document. I'm not going to tender the document. I would just like to put two or three questions. After that, we can give it a number, and after that, as soon as the translation comes in, then we are officially going to hand it over to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. There is a reason for the lack of translation so we will allow that to happen. What would the number be, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Interpretation) D4/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No doubt the Defence will make a copy available to us ahead of the translation because it may be of some value to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Make sure the Prosecution have a copy. In fact, they should probably have it. Have you one available?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let them have one now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Could the usher please take care of this? Your Honour, perhaps in order to speed up our work, I think that the witness should also look at a copy so that I could do this properly with him and then we will move more speedily, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could a copy please be placed on the ELMO for the interpreters, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: A copy on the ELMO for the interpreters, if you have one?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the usher help us, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I would like to continue, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness Zlotrg, we'll try to save a bit of time. Perhaps you would like to look at the document a bit more. Perhaps we can move on. I'm not going to go into any great detail with this record because it is going to be tendered into evidence. But just a few brief questions so that we see what all of this is about. The first sentence after the title of the document, that is to say, after the actual title, which is "Record of Investigation," the date and place is mentioned of the investigation and then further on it says in this sentence, "And on the occasion of the murder of Trako Samir," et cetera. Is there any doubt as to the relationship between this document and the event that we spoke of?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, most probably yes because I didn't write it, it is the judge who wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But the date is right, is it?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I assume it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what about the place?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the place is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what about the persons who were present?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The persons who are mentioned here are under the heading "Uvidjaj vrse ..." "The investigation is carried out by ..."

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Then the following heading is "General Facts."

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: For the purposes of the transcript, it says on the top of this page, "On the 22nd of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Oh, you're talking about this record?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. At 7.30 in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The record was written later. It was written by the judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But then it bears the date of the investigation itself.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, it says here the record was composed on the 22nd of May, 1992, and I know that the judge did not write it as we were there on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: As a criminology technician, I imagine that you attended a great many investigations before.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And there was an investigating judge there and he was in charge; right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And now you said that you assume that the judge wrote the record later ...

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Please, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it normal for the judge to write this later or does he write the same day or the very same minute? Tell us what was customary?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: He would write it on the same day. He would do it in handwriting. But here it says that it is composed, not that it was written on that date; that is to say, that it was typed out on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the judge dictated this to his secretary?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: That I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was the judge at the investigation, on-scene investigation?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you don't know exactly when he wrote it?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't, but at any rating, he couldn't have written it at 7.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On that morning, when you were there at 7.30, was he taking notes?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the first paragraph entitled "Opsti Podaci," general facts, and in the second half of this paragraph, approximately, after the address is mentioned, the address of the late Samir Trako, after the comma, it says, "The mentioned person was killed by a perpetrator known, Perica Vukadinovic," and then his personal data are given. On which basis did the investigating judge find out what the name of the person who did the shooting was?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was doing the investigation, and the judge was taking statements operationally. I did not know who he took statements from; I imagine from the commander of the military police, but I don't know. I was not present. But he did take statements from those present; that's what he was supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the penultimate paragraph, under the same heading but page 2, the paragraph begins with the words "a licu mjesta" or on the spot. It's more or less midway down the page. I shall read this sentence: "On the scene or on the spot, we found the eyewitnesses to the event, namely, Dubravko Kraljevic," I'll skip his personal particulars and address because we don't really need it now, then "Josip Tomic, Ratko Biletic, Ivan Budimir," and then the text goes on, "and eyewitnesses Trako Suad," and then again comes his particulars, "and Senad Petak were not found at the scene." The last sentence, the last sentence under this heading says, "Eyewitness Anastazija Blazevic was also found at the scene." Can you tell us, do you know the profession of any of these eyewitnesses or who they are, what they are, and how they happened to be there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not an operative worker; I'm a criminology technician, so it was up to me to collect evidence, and it was for others, together with the judge, to take the particulars and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. I was not asking you about your contacts and statements there. All I asked you was, we have just read the names of those persons, and all I want to ask you is, if you can tell us, whom among them do you know? Will you please just tell me the names of those you know?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Senad Petak, Ivan Budimir, and this one, Kraljevic, Dubravko, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you did not know Tomic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Suad Trako, you didn't know him?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure I know them, but now -- I mean, I listened to the names. These are the only ones I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Anastazija Blazevic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know that she owned that coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You don't know that?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, one could ask very many questions on the basis of this document, but I think it is telling enough as it is, so that I won't go into it further at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you spoke about some evidence at the scene of the crime, and, among other things, you mentioned blood, that is, blood stains on the floor of the room that we talked about. Then you said, if I may quote you, that in your view, "There should have been more blood."

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No. Wait for me to ask the question. Did I interpret correctly what you said?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And on the basis of what did you think that there should have been more blood?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is because they were perforating wounds because there were these marks through the glass wall, and the exit wound, that is, the bullet, as it comes out of the body, it makes a larger opening. Since the distance was four or five metres, there should have been more blood. I mean, there should have been blood throughout -- all along the corridor as they were carrying him out, and yet there were no more traces of blood, except for what I wrote down, just a very small -- there were very few traces of blood, and that is not logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, the body, was it or was it not there when you arrived there? Please, "Yes" or "No" only.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So how did you know at that moment where he received his wounds and whether it was a perforating wound? Where was the entry and exit wound? You can't know that.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Also, according to the statement and the position which they told us, they told us where the body was, and the door was slightly ajar. The witness, it means, was in the room, and the door is behind the witness. So if he is in the room, then the glass wall must have been behind him. Therefore, it must have been a perforating wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But that was your assumption?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness, a while ago, you said that you did your technical work and that you cannot go into the statements made by those present.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but we most know something about the event so as to do that. We must have some data as to where the body lay so as to perform other on-site investigation activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I see. That means that these conjectures were based on statements of others and on the basis of evidence?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So the conclusions did not derive only from criminology evidence, did they, but also were based on what other persons said?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for me, it is a good time for a break, but it's up to you. I can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're finishing early. Are you moving off this topic now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. This topic is finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In connection with your previous statements, to be precise, the first one with the judge in Zenica on the 3rd of October, '94 where you made your first statement, the first one we have, and then you made a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal on the 27th and 28th of September, '97 in connection with the events that we spoke about it, that is to say, the murder of Samir Trako, there is a difference which I'd like you to explain. When you made your statement to the investigating judge in Zenica, that is to say, on the 3rd of October, '94, you said that you could not ascertain who the perpetrator of the murder was but that there were rumours to the effect that Mario Cerkez, commander of the Vitez Brigade, was the perpetrator; is that true? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but I told the judge that I could not remember the name of the member of the military police who allegedly, that is, I imagine according to even Budimir, said that Perica Vukadinovic had committed that. That is what I found out later, that is to say, after a certain period of time, rumour had it in town that Mario Cerkez had killed this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I understand. But you told the judge in Zenica what I told you, what I read?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not read my statement in Zenica, so I don't know what ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, look, at the end of the statement you made in that court, there is a warning or, rather, a note to the effect that -- well, I'm really translating it from English: "That is all I have to say at this point in time, although many more things happened. Everything I said has been recorded accordingly. I have no objections and acknowledge this statement as mine with my signature." I don't think that it is very important, but I just asked you to confirm or deny, that is to say, just say "Yes" or "No," that you told the judge in Zenica that you were not able to ascertain who the perpetrator was but that rumour had it that it was Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I accept what was signed because at that point in time, Mr. Perica Vukadinovic was not accessible to us. He had been put away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigator of this Tribunal, the one that you made at the time I mentioned, namely, the 27th and the 28th of September, 1997, you explained this event in quite a bit of detail, and you do not mention here this story, this rumour that you heard, that Mario Cerkez had committed this; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but this is not a statement made to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What is it then?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is an official note, I think that is what it says up there, and it is some kind of a reminder for me. These were notes I offered to the investigator when he came to take a statement from me for the Aleksovski case. I mean, I can read you the original. See? Look. "Official note made on the 5th of September, 1996 on the occasion of --" I mean, that's what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Sorry. I asked you about the statement you made to the investigator on the 27th and 28th of September, 1997.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, possibly. I don't know. I thought --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me rephrase the question. Do you remember that in this statement you made to the investigator of the Tribunal, you did not mention at any point that you heard rumours to the effect that Cerkez was the perpetrator of this crime?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Had he asked me, I'm sure that I would have told him that he was the perpetrator. I gave a lot of statements, so I really do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Tell me a bit about the jurisdiction of courts in the territory of Vitez. As regards the event that we just talked about, you mentioned or, rather, we saw from the document itself that the judge from the basic court in Travnik came, and yesterday when you were telling us about another event, you mentioned that there was a judge from Zenica?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What was the territorial jurisdiction exactly of the courts that covered the territory of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. I'm not competent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can I infer then that in the case of one event, the Travnik court would be present and in another case, the Zenica court would be present?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, because when death is the outcome, then the judge of the higher court, of the basic court, has to come to the scene of the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Fine. I am asking you this for those who did not live there with us. Which one was the higher court, the one in Zenica or the one in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you can tell by the very name, the court in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So the court in Zenica was higher?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Wasn't that court supposed to be present then in the case of this murder?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know whether they authorised the basic court in Travnik. This is not within my own competence. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: As a criminology technician, that is to say, as part of the police, did you know that there were instructions issued by the Ministry that a higher court could assign a lower court to do certain things on their behalf?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, I'm going to interrupt you because we have spent a very long time on one particular incident. Now, it's for you to decide how to cross-examine, and I don't know what other material you want to put to the witness, but what I ask is this: Is this Trial Chamber going to be assisted with a very lengthy cross-examination on one particular topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. President, this last question or these last questions that were related in a way to the subject of the murder were actually aimed in a different direction. I am actually trying to show an order or, rather, a disorder that prevailed in this area, and I think that this is important because the witness presented the question of the legal order in a rather one-sided fashion in the municipality of Vitez. I don't want to dwell on the murder any longer, but the fact was that there were two different courts that were in charge of investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Kovacic, I think that the Judges are very well aware of your concerns. The problem is as follows: We might ask you to go straight to the core of what you want to present. You have your own strategy, haven't you, and it is up to you to present it, but you are also free to go straight to the topic to make the cross-examination easier. So this is the kind of contribution that we are expecting from you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Of course, I'll try, Your Honour, but it depends upon how cooperative the witness is too. Unfortunately, we had to repeat certain things; otherwise, there was no need to do so, really, but let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Zlotrg, when a crime would be committed in the territory of Vitez during this time that we are talking about, for example, from the mid -- from mid '92 or in the middle of 1992, who was in charge of arresting the perpetrator? We were just mentioning this by way of an example. It can be any other thing.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: If it was a civilian, then the civilian police; if it was a case of a member of the military, then the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when you would come to an investigation of a crime scene, if anybody would report to the police station, any citizen, that a crime had been committed, then the investigation team would go out, and -- we also saw this from part of your testimony yesterday -- quite often the persons involved are sometimes members of the military and sometimes they are civilians. How was a distinction made between civilian authority, that is to say, the powers of the civilian police, what they were supposed to do by way of carrying out the investigation in relation to what the military police were supposed to do with regard to crimes? Can you explain this to us in two or three words?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you please clarify this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you come to carry out an investigation of a crime scene and when you see that the victim is a soldier, will the civilian police continue the investigation or will it report to the military police about this event?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: When there is a report, then the police patrol goes to the scene and reports to the duty officer saying what it's all about, and then they immediately present the picture if he says, from the scene itself, whether this is a member of the military or whether it's a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So if the patrol in any way ...

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I'm not the one who decided what the composition of the investigation team would be. It was up to the duty officer to make the call to the right place and to the persons who were on duty in the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, that I understand.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm only part of the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, we've understood that. Perhaps I didn't put my question properly. What is the criterion, irrespective of who is doing this, the duty officer or the investigating team, for determining which police is in charge of a certain event, a certain crime?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it depends whose member this is, if this is a member of a certain army or if this person is a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, who? Who is a member of what?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes, I mean, it depends who did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, so you're trying to say the participants in the entire event?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You use plural, you said military police, that is units, so we had several military police forces and several units, and that transpires also from what you said yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, there was one civilian police and two military police forces, the military police of the Croatian Defence Council and the military police of the Territorial Defence headquarters in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Correct. During a period of time.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But later on, in late '92?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: In late November '92, when we were expelled from the police station and we were authorised by the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo, then we set up the Public Security Station loyal to the local government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So at that time and for the months to come, there were two civilian, two military --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- which operated in the same area.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The territories under the control of the Croatian Defence Council were controlled by the Croatian civilian police, and the territory where there was a majority Muslim population was under our control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I see. So does that mean that yesterday, when you read and we followed the events in sequence, and I think there are 37 incidents that are mentioned there, and all those acts that were read, in all of them Muslims were victims, were they not? Was that the result of that division or, rather, you, as police, as the civilian police of Stari Vitez, came out to conduct investigations only in the case of those incidents?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was taken from the report, that is, from the reports of -- from applications by citizens, and, naturally, it was citizens of Muslim ethnicity who came to our station, and we don't always go out for on-site investigation. We did not go out for on-site investigation when Hasan Skopljak was killed and robbed, and he was a well-off Muslim living in Bila, and there were quite a number of incidents when we did not conduct on-site investigation because those things happened in the territory controlled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So -- correct. So people from the area controlled by that station tried to --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, people from the town, they came to complain to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But then you could not conduct the on-site investigation, you couldn't go out?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, but we took record of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Is it possible that during that period when, that is, when those 37 [indiscernible] incidents came, that they had been between the 16th of December, '92 until mid April '93, is it possible that there was not a single Croat victim, that only Muslims fell prey to crime?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, I worked for the Public Security Station in Vitez, in Stari Vitez, and therefore this was the record of statements made by people who made applications, who came to report, and in all likelihood, Croats went to the station of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, but I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you do not know that during that time, some crimes had been committed at the expense of Croats?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't. I know that Croats came to us to get their driving lessons and plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Those who lived in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, those who lived in the town. They also came to apply for their passports to us and in large numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And still you do not know whether Croats were victims of crimes?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know because I had no access to the police station in the territory controlled by Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But does that mean that the civilian police in that part where you worked, that is, the civilian police in Stari Vitez, took care only about protecting Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, if I may, I should like to tender another document into evidence. Unfortunately, Judge Bennouna, we have not yet received a French translation -- some do have French translations, some do not, but these are quite straightforward documents, so perhaps it can be simple -- some of them were tendered in the Blaskic case at a later date, and all these documents that I will show now have already been tendered into evidence in the Blaskic case. Mr. Usher, will you please see that these documents are received by their Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Exhibit D5/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
