utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, at the top, you have the Croatian text and then it is followed by the English. Would the registrar please give a copy to the other Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you please turn to page 2 of the report?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could it please be placed on the ELMO for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The signature shows that the document was signed by Mr. Ivan Budimir. Is that the same person that you mentioned was present at that on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, if he doesn't have a double, then that was the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But could you conclude that that is the same person from the kind of activity that he was involved in?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the time when I knew him, he did not work for the SIS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell the Court what SIS stands for, if you know that?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: It means the Security and Information Service of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you now please go back to the first page, 1, and look at the heading? So if the person signing the document, Mr. Ivan Budimir, Intelligence Service, here we see who this Intelligence Service belonged to.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I also know that Mr. Zeljko Budimir was our General. Now he is with the Croatian army, a General again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please, will you stick to my questions and the Prosecutor may ask you some additional questions and then you may make statements that you like. Can you please identify which unit did, according to this document, belong the undersigned? What does the heading say?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade Commander, 2nd Vitez Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The document is entitled "Analysis," and then it says, "Analysis of the work of the military police in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Battalion." Do you know what was this 2nd Battalion and what was its zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Then let us look at the contents. Item 1, and the author says: "1. The following police forces exist in Vitez: the regional military police, the municipal military police, the 4th Military Police Battalion, and the civilian police." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know what period of time this is about because there is no date here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is true, there is no date. That's why I'm reading this out to you. Can you, from this structure, rather, this listing of military police forces, can we guess the date?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it should be late December '92 or early '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Correct. We agree on this. Then item 3 says: 3. Despite the presence of these four police forces, problems abound throughout the municipality of Vitez. And then, in item 4, there is mention of looting of cars, houses, of companies, woundings, subversive activities in the town, et cetera. You were with the police at the time, and you told us what you knew about Stari Vitez. Can you read from this? Can you say something about this, this information about very many crimes, very many offences, not in Stari Vitez alone and not in Vitez alone?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but these are mostly Muslim facilities, and I listed dates and names of the owners. What it says here is only cafes whereas I specified dates and addresses, that is, Kolonija, the urban part of the town controlled by the Croatian Council of Vitez, and I think it quite tallies with my list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, quite. I have no doubts as to that they tally. Quite the contrary. What I'm asking is, can you conclude from this that on the Croat side, somebody was also concerned about crime?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but the situation was getting worse with every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. You said that your police had moved, when it began working again in Stari Vitez, to the fire brigade building.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. To begin with, it is not my police, and will you, please, sir -- that was the police of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina loyal to the local government, so, please, do not call it as my personal police. I have always, with all due respect, I always said the police of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and I think it is really not proper to say that either with regard to myself or the state that I come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. It was not deliberate. I simply tried to make things shorter. So the police for which you worked, the police of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I really did not try to say anything, but be that as it may, when it began working again, I mean, the police for which you worked, that was the police under the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, then your offices and your seat, your headquarters, was in the fire brigade building in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, next to the fire brigade building, there is another building. That is where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what did you have in the fire brigade building? That is the same compound, is it not?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: They have nothing to do --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they are two different, two separate buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So what was in the fire brigade building?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the same thing as in '91 and 1990. Those were the premises of the fire brigade coffee shop run by a Croat. I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So let me ask you: After the 8th of January, '93, whose were the premises? Whose were the offices in the fire brigade in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, nobody. I mean, of the political or the police, nobody had offices there, as far as I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the police that you worked for was in the building next to it?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was in the building next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the fire brigade, before the beginning of the conflict, were the Croats and Muslims represented on a par?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: That you would have to ask somebody from the fire brigade because I was not a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know, after January '93, did Croats continue to work in the fire brigade building?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, our fire brigade was on a voluntary basis. There were no professional firemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But did Croats come to the fire brigade building?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had no time to really look at something like that, but if they could come to our police station to apply for a passport, then I guess they also went to the fire brigade building. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness, let me ask you a direct question: Did members of the BH army, on the 8th of January, '93, if you remember, or at any time, if you remember, just tell me "Yes" or "No," did they ever take over the fire brigade building from the firemen?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, the command of the BH army was right at the opposite end of Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is true, but did they occupy this building, tell me "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not a member of the Armija, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you were in the building next to it?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I wish to tender into evidence another document. Unfortunately, this document has not been translated. We also ask for it together with the record of the on-site investigation. But this is a short document. Perhaps it would be best to read it out. Perhaps we should reserve a number and we shall subsequently submit the translation. It is only one paragraph, some five or six lines altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Make sure there is a copy put on the ELMO for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And for the Prosecution, if we may have one directly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Interpretation) This is Exhibit D6/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Please, could the other Defence team also get a copy? I omitted to provide them with one. Your Honours, I'm not sure what is the fastest and simplest way to proceed, but I imagine that the best thing would be for me to read this out slowly so that we can hear the interpretation of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The heading says "The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Defence Council, the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, the 2nd Battalion, Vitez." The date, 8th of January, 1993. That's the date that you can see. And the document is entitled "Official Note." The text reads as follows: "On the 8th of January, 1993, at 12.45, I was informed by the Military Police, the active force of the Military Police from Vitez, over the telephone that around 11.00, the members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina --" It is abbreviated here "the BH army." "-- took the former premises of the fire brigade of Vitez, namely, the upstairs premises and the control room for the firemen from which the alert for fires is sounded, and by virtue of that, they exercised control over the vehicles of the fire brigade too." The second paragraph reads as follows: "On the basis of information received to date, I know that all firemen are volunteers and that there are only two Muslims among them, and all the rest are Croats." Above the signature, it says: "Notes made by the commander of the 2nd Battalion, Vitez, Anto Bertovic." Witness, tell me, please, yesterday you mentioned that at one point in time the Croats wanted to get the vehicles when there was a fire but that they were not allowed to do so. What was all of that about?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the explosive was planted in the premises of the Privredna Banka bank office in Vitez, to the best of my knowledge, Marijan Strukar, who was commander -- I don't know exactly, I was not a member of this voluntary fire brigade association, so I don't know exactly what their chain of command is -- he tried to take advantage of this explosion, although there were no reports stating that there was a fire down there or whatever. He got all of the vehicles of the fire brigade out of the garages and took them down to Vitez. That is on the basis of the information that I received. Could I please comment on this official note a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No. I'm going to put questions to you and then --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: But there are quite a few illogical things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now you're going to answer my questions, and my colleague, the Prosecutor, can ask you whatever you wanted to be asked. Yesterday, when you started your testimony, you said that Pero Skopljak, chief of police, was bringing in weapons from Herzegovina and that, in this connection, Cosic objected to you and asked you why you Muslims were not preparing for war too.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that was the drift of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Exactly. Exactly. That was the sense in which this question was put. Could you tell us exactly when this conversation took place, approximately?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: On several occasions before I handed over the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So that's the end of '91, the beginning of '92?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, no, this was in '91.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, '91. So it was around '91. Okay. Did you already see on television then or in the newspapers or did you know that the former JNA had already attacked Slovenia, the war already started in Croatia, and in the beginning of '92, there were already problems in Bosnia? Were you aware of that fact then?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You lived in Vitez, in Central Bosnia. The war had not reached that area yet.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: But we watched the news.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you were aware of the war that was on the threshold?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps had a wise policy been pursued, there would not have been a war. Macedonia did not have a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, that's your opinion.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It's your opinion too that war was on the threshold. We do not know then what would happen. That was the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. I agree. Somebody had made this assessment and somebody had not. I agree. But were there any military preparations in Bosnia for the war that would come?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Those states that were on the borders, that is to say, Serbia and Croatia, helped their own people. Unfortunately, we did not have that kind of a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You were in charge of materiel and weapons at that time, including the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. All the weapons and ammunition and equipment were in my hands, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When were they handed out?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the reserve police force was mobilised. I don't know the exact date. These documents should be in the Public Security Station if they did not destroy the documents after they kicked us out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you at least give us an approximate time for this?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were so many events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I would like to tender into evidence another document. This is only a list, a list of names. I put the headings there myself because there's nothing to translate. There are ten words all together that should be translated, so I did this myself by hand. Of course, this is an unofficial translation, and later we shall add the translation to it too. Could the usher please assist?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Interpreted) this is D7/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just going to ask you to take a look at this list, the heading. Unfortunately, it doesn't have a date; it doesn't have a signature. Tell me, please, could this be one of the lists or the list or a list related to the reserve police force that you were talking about and that was issued weapons?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, the papers I gave out were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No. I did not mean the papers that you personally gave out because I could not see that on any basis. But when you look at the names, the serial numbers, the models of weapons, could this be related to the members of the reserve police force or part of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this document doesn't say a thing to you?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: It only says to me that the Muslims were armed with these weapons, nothing else. And who made this list, that, I do not know. Anybody could have made this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) In this connection, Your Honours, I would like the witness to assist us in another matter. Could the usher please show him a map, put a map in front of him?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Interpreted) Exhibit D8/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Zlotrg, before we look at the map, in relation to this list of the reserve police, all those names or almost all those names on the list, could they be Muslim names?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are all Muslim, as far as I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. The majority, we could say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I think I owe you an apology. This is my translation. It's not really a translation. It's only here to help us. In the glossary that the Prosecutor was so kind to give us, all the acronyms, all the abbreviations used in this document, that is, all these acronyms we see in the middle column and which were indicating the type of weapon, such as "PM" or "AP," and then in the last column before figures, these letters "BK," all these can be found in that glossary. I think I can explain that, but I don't think there's any need for that, because these are only types of armaments, and "BK" means the combat set of ammunition, I believe, but you can see it for yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let us now turn back to the map. The reserve police, and bearing in mind this list and the villages indicated there, could you use your marker --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Usher, will you please give a marker to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Of course, nobody can remember all the details, but to the best of your recollection, could you please indicate places where the reserve force units should have been deployed?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had only two reserve police stations. They are the premises of the Automotive Club in Vitez at the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You mean in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, down at the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps show us where it is because the map is rather large? Roughly, approximately, could you just put a small red circle in that part of the town?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the second one was?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment. The second one was in the elementary school in Bila, that is, at Divjak, at Mecava, which should be somewhere here, the elementary school. There were only two stations of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. This plan of activity of the reserve police force, did that plan envisage also some smaller mobile teams which would only have a base at a different road or place or somewhere?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't really know. It was not under my competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you mean these places are physical bases. I'm talking about armaments, you know, the equipment?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: To those two places, I went for equipment and armaments for members of these two police stations. If I'm correct, the commander was Ivan Budimir, and he was the one who signed the receipt, but I can't really remember it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But there was a distribution.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and there was equipment which was [indiscernible] police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You mentioned one of the commanders --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The same problem has recurred, there is no discrimination between "Question" and "Answer," and LiveNote is concerned about its ability to serve the Court and us properly, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, could you remember, and Mr. Zlotrg, could you allow time for the translation before you reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I do apologise. I shall do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zlotrg, you heard. We've both been reprimanded, and the problem is that we are both speaking the same language. So if I may try to sum up where we went wrong, and will you please answer only "Yes" or "No"? From this part of the interview, it transpired that you knew that there were two places as seats of the reserve police, and those two places were marked by you on the map, and you identify them because, in view of your job, that is, the person responsible for materiel and equipment, you took weapons to them. Is the answer "Yes"?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The second thing when we went too fast, you are not aware of the further distribution or deployment of groups or teams of the reserve police forces in the territory of the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you don't know. Thank you. I believe you mentioned that at one of those places a reserve policeman or, rather, the leader of that group or that place was Mr. Budimir?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was the commander of the reserve police force in the elementary school which was at Mecava, at Petar Mecava.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, how many weapons did you give them, roughly, the order of magnitude?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, half of it went to each of the stations, so I -- 50 per cent went to one station and 50 per cent to the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But the order of magnitude?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: It went 50-50.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Who was in the other station? I mean, what person?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I know that for a while, the commander was Mirsad Tatarevic, but whether he was still there at that time, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If it was Mirsad -- I repeat, if it was Mirsad -- do you know if he was a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Muslim. Budimir is a Croat. So just for parity's sake, I presume that the other one was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know, do you remember who was the commander of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were directly subordinated to the station commander, Mr. Saban Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was it perhaps a military secret?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: They wore uniforms around the town and performed police business, so it was no secret. We are public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you of the name Mirhad Rebisic. Does that name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As for the -- you mean the work?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I mean the post.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As for the police work, he had absolutely nothing to do with us and he was not employed by the Public Security Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, we know that. But was he perhaps commander of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I just told you. Mr. Budimir and Tatarevic, they had only one commander and that was Mr. Saban Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. I see. So your commander.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to that disorder -- and that is my interpretation at least -- in this situation in Vitez in early 1993, and you told us something about that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, we should like to introduce into evidence another document. Mr. Usher, will you please help us? There is a translation. Unfortunately, Judge Bennouna, the French translation is missing, and I'm quite positive that one or two have been translated into French, but we shall submit them the moment we get those translations. It is a simple document anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D9/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, it's almost half past twelve and we shall be adjourning then, so it may be convenient when you've dealt with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Providing, of course, Your Honours, if I may just mention that there should be a standard warning that there will not be contact between the Prosecution and the witness since I already offered the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want to deal -- why don't you deal with the document briefly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will really briefly and I will leave it. As the document is, I would just ask:

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Did you have time to look through this document? Just to be sure that you understand the document, let me just tell you the subject of this document.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The problems the police faced in relation to some crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is that your impression, when reading this document, that the author of the document is worried about the crime rate in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Another question: Is the person who undersigned this document -- unfortunately, it seems that we lost it in copying -- but is that that same Ivan Budimir who was the reserve policeman? Is that again him?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I guess so because I do not know any other Ivan Budimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So can we reasonably conclude that the reserve policeman is writing the report and is dealing with crime in the --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: He is the commander of the reserve police force and he has not been appointed head of the police by accident and who was trained to do this kind of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Is he a Croat?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Do you anticipate being very much longer with this witness, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guess I will be able to close within one hour, perhaps a little bit more than an hour. But it's really difficult. I mean, don't catch me for word. That's my best estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Because he clearly should be able to leave as early as possible. I don't know whether the other Defence lawyers are going to be very long with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: I will be paring it down over the weekend, but at least 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Following on yesterday's issue, it might be desirable to have a one-minute, whatever it's called, private session now, which is easy to accomplish, so that the record is complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: As far as the witness is concerned, he is released. You don't want him to remain?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is one matter briefly I want to ... Mr. Zlotrg, I'm sorry you have got to remain here over a long weekend. Could you be back on Monday at 3.00, and I hope we shall be able to finish your evidence. Remember, please, not to speak to anybody, of course, about it. If you would like to go now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, before we go into private session, or as we go in, could you let us know this: We asked at one stage for a revised list of witnesses, pruned down, we anticipated. We are anxious to get to this area of our work and we need your document. When are you likely to have it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 12.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of May, 1999, at 3.00 p.m.
